question: What verifiable regional fishery and taxon leads does the BFAR Leyte Gulf 2001-2011 assessment provide, and can they support current occurrence or catch guidance?

sourceReviewed.citation: Francisco, M. C., Dayap, N. A., Tumabiene, L. A., Francisco, R. A., Sr., Candole, M. J., De Veyra, J. H., & Bautista, E. (2018). Status of Leyte Gulf Fisheries CYs 2001-2011. The Philippine Journal of Fisheries, 25(1), 136-155. https://doi.org/10.31398/tpjf/25.1.2017C0011
sourceReviewed.access: Reviewed the official DA-NFRDI repository record and its full 20-page PDF of the BFAR-authored Philippine Journal of Fisheries article.

reportedScope.waterbody: Marine Leyte Gulf and San Pedro Bay region spanning landing centers in Leyte and Eastern Samar; not an inland-water inventory or legal-boundary source.
reportedScope.studyWindow: National Stock Assessment Program monitored-landing data covering calendar years 2001-2011.
reportedScope.landingSites: The Methods names Sto. Niño and Abuyog (Leyte); Taraguna, McArthur (Leyte); Rizal and San Jose, Dulag; Bislig and San Roque, Tanauan; Lupok and Public Market, Guiuan (Eastern Samar); Balangiga and Lawaan, Salcedo (Eastern Samar) for 2002-2007; and San Jose, Tacloban added in 2008. This is 10 named centers at a time only if the stated time-dependent coverage is resolved; do not infer one fixed complete panel.
reportedScope.samplingMethod: Monitored boat landings at intervals of two days, targeting 10-11 sampling days monthly at each sampling area. Catch, gear, effort, landing center/fishing ground and species-composition subsamples were collected; this is fishery landing monitoring, not a spatially balanced biological survey.
reportedScope.reportedAggregates: The article reports 38 gear types and aggregate production/CPUE summaries. It calls its 2001-2011 catch grouping 142 'families' and then lists animal-group counts of 106 finfishes, 5 crustaceans, 7 mollusks, 6 shellfish, and 1 sea cucumber; the wording and arithmetic do not reconcile. It also says municipal and commercial fishers 'totaled' 809 and 293 species, respectively, without a machine-readable underlying taxon/landing dataset to interpret those numbers as unique taxa.
reportedScope.nameAndTableCaveats: These are verbatim distinct scientific-name strings appearing in Table 3's top-ten lists for 2001, 2006 and 2011, not a complete checklist. Portunus pelagicus is a crab, not a fish. The article prints 'Ratsrelliger kanagurta' and labels Gazza minuta with 'Leoignathidae' in the table; preserve source strings and do not silently normalize spelling or family. Table 3 also has other taxonomic-label inconsistencies that need specialist review.
reportedScope.historicalInterpretation: All catch, CPUE, seasonality, size and gear comparisons describe the 2001-2011 assessment period and its landing-monitoring design. They are not current presence, abundance, fishing conditions, legal rules, safety status or recreational catchability guidance.

crossSourceAssessment.habitatScope: Marine capture-fishery data only; no freshwater, brackish-water delineation, river/lake records or municipal-water geometry derived.
crossSourceAssessment.timeAndSamplingLimit: An eleven-calendar-year historical landing series does not establish present-day local occupancy or abundance and is influenced by gears, ports, fishing grounds and reporting design.
crossSourceAssessment.taxonomyReadiness: Table 3 is a selected top-ten extract for three comparison years, includes a crustacean, and contains visibly inconsistent source spellings/family labels. Keep verbatim source-name leads separate from accepted taxa and specimen-linked occurrences.
crossSourceAssessment.appReadiness: Useful historical regional fisheries context and discovery lead only. The article does not furnish a verified current species-by-site occurrence feed, current catchability, current law/safety guidance, diet evidence, or publication permission for a Bangwit data projection.

rightsReview.status: No item-specific open license was identified on the inspected NFRDI record or in the article PDF.
rightsReview.handling: Retain citation and concise factual summary; do not copy tables, figures, article pages, or aggregate datasets into app data. Preserve source-printed names as research leads only.

disposition.reason: Historical landing-monitoring data contain unresolved category/count and printed-name issues, lack a reusable machine-readable underlying taxon-by-place dataset, and do not establish current occurrence or recreational guidance.

nextActions: Keep this 2001-2011 Leyte Gulf assessment linked to the separate 2020 trawl paper without treating their designs, species counts, stations, or periods as interchangeable.

If taxon names are later promoted, first preserve the original printed strings, independently crosswalk each name/family, confirm the landing-site/fishing-ground definition, and resolve Table 3 anomalies.
Continue Eastern Visayas freshwater and brackish discovery separately for Leyte, Samar, and Biliran; do not infer regional completeness from marine fishery statistics.

sources.supports: Official DA-NFRDI repository record: publisher, 2018 issue, author list and the downloadable BFAR-authored article PDF.
Full paper text reviewed for 2001-2011 monitored landing methods and sites, aggregate claims, Table 3 source-name leads, gear/time results, and internal table/category caveats.
